CVE-2015-5477.title: BIND TKEY assertion failure: establish exposure without crashing DNS
CVE-2015-5477.summary: A TKEY packet-handling defect can terminate named. Both recursive and authoritative BIND servers are affected, and the vulnerable path runs before DNS ACL/service-policy checks. A recursion restriction is therefore not evidence that this defect is mitigated.
CVE-2015-5477.affected: ISC advisory: 9.1.0–9.8.x; 9.9.0–9.9.7-P1; 9.10.0–9.10.2-P2. Historical fixed releases: 9.9.7-P2 and 9.10.2-P3. These old fixed releases are not a recommendation to deploy an unsupported release today; use a supported vendor build with the fix or a documented distribution backport.

discover.title: Collect the local deployed BIND identity
discover.code:
# On the approved DNS host; no crafted DNS packet is sent.
named -v
command -v dpkg-query >/dev/null && dpkg-query -W 'bind9*'
command -v rpm >/dev/null && rpm -qa 'bind*'
discover.interpretation: Record the actual running binary/package and distribution revision. A different PATH binary or package version is insufficient if named runs from a container, bundled appliance or alternate installation.

verify: Establish DNS reachability from the recorded external/internal vantage point using existing flow/configuration evidence or an ordinary approved DNS lookup. DNS success is service evidence, not CVE proof.

Compare the running named build with the exact branch-specific affected ranges above. For vendor-packaged builds, obtain the package erratum/backport record; do not compare distribution version strings as upstream versions.

If an affected build lacks a documented fix, record the vulnerable-version exposure. Do not count recursive-query ACLs as fixing this defect, because the vendor explicitly states the vulnerable path precedes those checks.
This guide verifies applicability, not a disruptive TKEY reproduction. The observable historical failure is a REQUIRE assertion and daemon exit, but an unrelated named crash does not prove this CVE.
fix: Install a supported BIND or appliance/distribution update that includes this fix. ISC lists no application workaround for this defect.
Restrict network reachability to required DNS clients where operationally possible while updating, but do not substitute DNS ACL settings for the update.
Ensure the running process is using the updated binary, not merely an updated file on disk.
retest: Repeat named/build/package evidence after the required service restart and reconcile it with the vendor-fixed build.
Perform normal recursive/authoritative lookups required by this server's role and check service stability and logs. Record each tested role rather than assuming one lookup covers all behavior.
detection: Correlate named assertion failures, unexpected exits/restarts and DNS availability failures with the deployed build and request time. Do not call every assertion this CVE.
Check that process-exit/availability alerts reach responders and distinguish a test-induced failure from a historical incident.

CVE-2016-3081.title: Struts S2-032: verify Dynamic Method Invocation and fix the mapper boundary
CVE-2016-3081.summary: Remote expression evaluation is possible through dynamic method selection when Dynamic Method Invocation (DMI) is enabled. Product/version evidence and the effective DMI configuration are both needed; a Struts-looking page does not prove this condition.
CVE-2016-3081.affected: Apache S2-032 lists Struts 2.3.20–2.3.28 except 2.3.20.3 and 2.3.24.3; historical fixed releases are 2.3.20.3, 2.3.24.3 and 2.3.28.1. NVD's description/configuration entries differ in some older versions. Preserve that discrepancy and use the vendor/package advisory for the deployed branch rather than treating the flattened NVD list as a verdict.

discover.title: Locate configuration overrides in the approved application directory
discover.code:
# Read-only; run from the actual deployed/extracted application configuration directory.
grep -R -n --include='struts.xml' --include='struts.properties' \
  'struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation' .
discover.interpretation: A match shows a declared setting, not effective runtime configuration. Inspect classpath overrides, packaged configuration and custom ActionMapper implementations. No match does not mean disabled.

verify: Identify the deployed struts-core artifact and exact package/build revision, including every application/worker using it.
Review the effective struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation constant and configuration precedence. The supported fixed-tag default is false, but application overrides may enable it.
If DMI is enabled on an affected unpatched build, record applicability. If it is demonstrably disabled, record that mitigation for this CVE without declaring all Struts vulnerabilities absent.
Use source/configuration evidence rather than submitting an expression or shell command. Review custom ActionMapper code against the supported fixed behavior.
fix: Disable DMI where the application allows it: <constant name="struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation" value="false"/> in struts.xml, or struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation=false in the effective properties configuration.
Update to a supported maintained Struts release with this and subsequent fixes. The 2.3.x historical fixed versions are historical evidence, not current lifecycle recommendations.
If custom mapping is required, review and test it against vendor-fixed behavior rather than trusting the default mapper setting alone.
retest: Recheck the deployed artifact and effective DMI setting after redeployment across all instances.
Exercise normal documented actions and confirm required routing still works. Inspect mapper/configuration regression tests; no RCE payload is required for this guide.
detection: Monitor unexpected action/method-selection failures and unusual application child processes with deployment/request correlation.
Log relevant route and decision metadata without retaining credentials or treating every invalid action name as a successful exploit.

code.note: Exact case-sensitive DMI key; defaults may be overridden.
Mapper gates dynamic selection and sanitizes the selected action method; this is source code, not an exploit.

CVE-2023-22894.title: Strapi private-field filtering: check applicability and search existing request logs
CVE-2023-22894.summary: Filtering on private user fields can disclose sensitive information indirectly. The vendor later identified unauthenticated paths and chaining risk, so the older admin-only NVD description/metric must not be used to exclude unauthenticated exposure.
CVE-2023-22894.affected: Vendor disclosure lists >=3.2.1,<4.8.0 and records the fix release as 4.8.0; its recommendation explicitly says upgrade beyond 4.8.0. The older NVD prose saying through 4.5.5 is incomplete. Prefer a currently supported newer release; v3 reached end of life and did not receive this fix.

discover.title: Identify installed Strapi packages
discover.code:
# From the deployed Strapi application directory; does not install packages.
npm ls @strapi/strapi @strapi/plugin-users-permissions --depth=0
discover.interpretation: Reconcile output with the running deployment and bundled artifacts. A source checkout or stale node_modules tree is not necessarily the running instance.

discover.title: Review existing logs without printing matching sensitive request contents
discover.code:
# Replace with an approved log copy. Prints matching line numbers only.
grep -niE '(\[|%5B)[[:space:]]*(email|password|reset_password_token|resetPasswordToken)[[:space:]]*(\]|%5D)' /approved/log-copy/access.log | cut -d: -f1
discover.interpretation: This adapts the vendor's indicator search. Matches are triage leads, not proof of disclosure; normal filters can match. Missing matches do not prove absence if query strings are omitted, logs were rotated or encoding differs. Keep original evidence restricted.

verify: Establish exact running Strapi version and supported branch. Apply the vendor range above rather than excluding builds based on the older NVD summary.
Inspect approved API/private-field configuration and code/patch evidence. Do not attempt to infer real password hashes or reset tokens.

Review existing logs for the documented private-field filter indicators and correlate repeated suspicious password/reset-token filters with identity and server behavior. Treat data-leak confirmation as an incident-response task, not an invitation to extract more data.
Use synthetic fixtures and vendor-supported regression tests to validate private fields cannot be filtered/read through applicable routes; preserve expected and actual decisions.
fix: Upgrade to a supported Strapi release newer than the vendor's 4.8.0 recommendation boundary; verify companion plugins and all running instances are updated.
Do not assume strapi/security-patches fixes this CVE: the repository reviewed here only contains CVE-2023-22621 patches.

If suspicious private-field filtering is confirmed, investigate possible token/credential disclosure and follow the organization's response process. Patching does not invalidate previously exposed secrets by itself.
retest: Recheck running versions, private-field configuration and synthetic regression cases across relevant public and authenticated routes.
Confirm legitimate allowed filters still function and inappropriate private-field access is rejected. Verify request/identity logging remains available without exposing secrets.
detection: Correlate repeated private password/reset-token filter requests with source identity, route and response behavior; the vendor highlights these requests as indicators.
Test alert ingestion using a labeled synthetic log event, separate from any data-disclosure reproduction. Do not promise every request variant is covered by one regex.

CVE-2023-22621.title: Strapi email-template SSTI: validate version, templates and the specific fix
CVE-2023-22621.summary: The users-permissions email-template system allowed server-side template execution. Version checks and template-integrity review can establish exposure without inserting executable template code. The plugin is installed by default according to the vendor.
CVE-2023-22621.affected: Vendor disclosure: all known v3 and v4 releases before 4.5.6 are affected. Fixed in 4.5.6 for this CVE, but the vendor strongly advises upgrading beyond 4.8.0 for related vulnerabilities. A CVE-2023-22621-only patch does not fix CVE-2023-22894 or CVE-2023-22893.

discover.title: Inventory deployed plugin revisions
discover.interpretation: For v3, identify the corresponding strapi-plugin-* packages through existing artifact/package evidence. This command is an inventory lead, not a template execution test.

verify: Record running Strapi/plugin versions and whether the documented fix is present in the deployed artifacts.

Review existing email templates and approved changes against the application's known-good templates; do not execute unfamiliar content. Preserve suspicious template versions through incident-response handling.
Review request logs for PUT /users-permissions/email-templates and correlate with legitimate administrator changes. This path alone indicates a template modification, not compromise.

Where a manual patch was used, compare exact target package versions and deployed patch contents against the vendor repository; a patch file in the source folder is not evidence that it applied successfully.
fix: Prefer upgrading to a currently supported release newer than the vendor's related-fix guidance rather than installing an old minimum version.

For a temporary vendor-supported CVE-only patch, use the exact matching release target in strapi/security-patches. The reviewed targets are 3.6.11, 4.0.8, 4.1.12, 4.2.3, 4.3.9 and 4.4.7. The repository requires patch-package/postinstall setup; mismatched versions must be reconciled first.
Remove or restore suspicious templates through an approved response procedure and investigate server effects if compromise is suspected.
retest: Verify updated running artifacts or successful version-matched patch application on every deployment.
Run vendor/developer template validation regression tests with benign fixtures and confirm normal reset/confirmation email rendering. Do not insert command-execution templates.
detection: Review unexpected email-template modifications and application child processes with actor/request correlation.
Retain template-change audit events and alert on changes outside the approved workflow; a legitimate template edit should not be treated automatically as an intrusion.

code.note: Users-permissions email templating fix; not a fix for all three Strapi CVEs.
Version-specific patch-package fixes; prefer a supported upgrade.

CVE-2023-22893.title: Strapi Cognito provider: verify provider use and JWKS-backed validation
CVE-2023-22893.summary: The users-permissions AWS Cognito provider had a token-verification weakness. The vendor says applications not using this provider are not impacted by this CVE. The Enterprise admin SSO system is a different authentication implementation.
CVE-2023-22893.affected: Vendor disclosure: >=3.2.1,<4.6.0; fixed in 4.6.0. Strapi v3 did not receive this fix. The vendor advises a newer release beyond 4.8.0 for other vulnerabilities.

discover.title: Inventory the deployed users-permissions package
discover.interpretation: Use effective provider configuration to establish Cognito use; package installation alone does not establish that this provider is enabled.

verify: Check exact deployed version and whether the users-permissions AWS Cognito provider is actually used. Keep admin Enterprise SSO separate.

Inspect the effective Cognito issuer/user-pool configuration and its configured JWKS URL. Record expected issuer/audience/key validation through supported configuration and regression-test evidence, not forged authentication tokens.
Review historical provider callback events using restricted logging/incident tools. Any token review must avoid copying raw tokens into this vault or app.
If provider configuration is unavailable, record applicability as unresolved; absence of a visible login button does not prove the provider is unused.
fix: Upgrade to a supported patched Strapi release, preferably beyond the vendor's related 4.8.0 guidance.
Configure the Cognito provider's JWKS URL after upgrading; the vendor says login will fail if it is omitted.
Do not apply CVE-2023-22621 patch-package files as a substitute: no CVE-2023-22893 fix was found in that reviewed repository.
retest: Confirm normal synthetic Cognito login works and documented negative token-validation regression tests reject invalid issuer/key/audience conditions.
Recheck the running version/provider configuration and identity-log visibility after deployment; redact tokens.
detection: Correlate Cognito callback events with verification failures and identity-provider audit events.
Distinguish authentication validation failure, ordinary misconfiguration and a confirmed account impact; follow response policy where historical unauthorized access is established.
